cells.value: Plan Mode is a read-only environment for designing solutions before implementation. The plan approval mode is a strict read-only mode for research and design, and in Plan Mode the agent is restricted to read-only tools.

general.defaultApprovalMode defaults to 'default', which prompts for approval on each tool call; the setting also covers auto_edit and plan. Plan Mode is enabled by default (as of v0.34.0) and can be managed via /settings.

The latest-stable changelog page is headed v0.61.0 and calls the latest stable release the recommended one for most users; the preview page is headed v0.63.0-preview.0. The releases page names the registry as the single source of truth for determining the current version.

cells.value: Gemini CLI has three major release channels: nightly, preview, and stable. The weekly release cadence promotes code from main -> nightly -> preview. Nightly releases run on a daily schedule.

To update a source checkout, pull the latest changes from the repository. Gemini CLI is officially available in the ACP Agent Registry, which lists "Latest versions" as ensuring users always have access to the most up-to-date version.

Release notes for all versions are published at /docs/changelogs. Changelog entries read "Changelog for v0.60.0-preview.0 by @gemini-cli-robot". The patch release workflow creates a new GitHub release with the patch notes.

cells.value: Gemini CLI's recommended system specifications list the operating systems macOS 15+, Windows 11 24H2+ and Ubuntu 20.04+, the runtime Node.js 20.0.0+, and the shells Bash, Zsh, or PowerShell.

Google AI Pro or Ultra subscribers automatically have higher limits for Gemini Code Assist and Gemini CLI, and 'these are shared across Gemini CLI' and agent mode in the IDE (quote truncated). Organization tiers apply when signing in with a Google Workspace account.
cells.limitation: Gemini for workspace plans: 'These plans do not apply to the API usage which powers the' Gemini CLI (E-gemini-cli-02090); organization tiers instead apply to Workspace sign-in (E-gemini-cli-00953).

cells.value: Token usage and cached token savings can be viewed with /stats. The headless JSON output carries a stats object with token usage and API latency metrics. A summary of model usage is presented on exit at the end of a session. Cached token information is only displayed when cached tokens are being used.

cells.value: billing.overageStrategy sets how to handle quota exhaustion when AI credits are available: 'ask' prompts each time, 'always' automatically uses credits, 'never' disables credit usage. The default is "ask".
cells.limitation: Scoped to "quota exhaustion when AI credits are available"; the options are ask (prompt each time), always (automatically use credits) or never (disable credit usage).

cells.value: For Log in with Google (Gemini Code Assist for individuals), the listed limit is 1000 maximum model requests / user / day. When rate-limited, the CLI automatically switches to the "flash" model. It tells you when you reach your Gemini 3 Pro daily usage limit. A 429 Resource exhausted error indicates the API request limit was exceeded.

Gemini CLI uses OpenTelemetry (OTel) to record traces that help debug agent behavior. The docs list a Telemetry feature with usage and performance metric details. Telemetry includes session.id, installation.id and active_approval_mode. Telemetry can be sent directly to Google Cloud.

--debug (-d) runs in debug mode with verbose logging (default false). /chat debug exports the most recent API request as a JSON payload. F12 toggles the debug console for detailed error information. general.debugKeystrokeLogging enables debug logging of keystrokes to the console.
